summary: AstroBricks AI is an interactive learning project that combines a LEGO lunar base with a digital mission app. Children guide two astronauts through an eight-day mission while learning how to manage essential resources such as solar energy, water, food, and oxygen, and how to protect astronauts from radiation. NFC tags connect LEGO structures to information about each station, helping children explore its purpose through hands-on play instead of spending all their time on a screen. The app tracks mission resources and shows whether the astronauts complete their mission successfully. By building and testing their own ideas, children can learn about space exploration, teamwork, and resource conservation. Their imaginative designs may also inspire new ideas for future space habitats and missions.
details:
AstroBricks AI: Build a Lunar Mission, One Choice at a Time

Imagine a child standing beside a lunar base they built with LEGO. Instead of only looking at a screen, they choose an astronaut, tap an NFC sticker on one of their buildings, and discover why that structure matters to the mission. AstroBricks AI combines an interactive app with hands-on LEGO building to help children explore how people could live and manage resources on the Moon.

The mission begins when the child chooses an astronaut, female or male, and starts an eight-day lunar survival simulation. Each day, the child monitors and manages essential resources: solar energy, food, water, and oxygen. They also learn how a radiation-protection shelter can help keep the astronaut safe.

As the mission progresses, the child may encounter challenges such as a solar storm, a water shortage, or lunar dust. They must decide how to respond and manage the available resources. Their choices affect the mission’s progress and the astronaut’s ability to continue. At the end of the eight days, the app shows whether the plan succeeded and lets the child try again with different decisions.

The LEGO model is part of the experience. The child places NFC stickers on buildings in the lunar base. Tapping a sticker opens information about that structure: its purpose, how it supports the crew, and how it is used during the mission. For example, the radiation-protection station explains why the astronaut may need a sheltered place during a radiation event.

The child can also use the app’s camera to take a photo of their LEGO model and attach it to the mission. The photo records what they built, while the NFC stickers connect each structure to its role in the lunar base.

I designed AstroBricks AI so children learn by building, exploring, and making decisions, with the screen supporting their play. They connect information in the app to something they can see and touch, then think about how to use resources responsibly. The building and mission information is based on materials provided through the challenge.

AstroBricks AI invites children to build a lunar base, manage its resources, and help an astronaut make it through eight days on the Moon—one thoughtful decision at a time.

The models children create may also spark ideas that adults have not yet considered. A child’s imagination can offer fresh ways to think about future lunar habitats, spacecraft, transportation, and pathways across the Moon. These designs could inspire scientists and engineers, including those at NASA, to explore new questions and possibilities for future space exploration. Children are not simply building models; they are sharing their own vision of what life in space might look like.
